scenes.title: One Photograph Too Many
scenes.narration: Nadia was preparing a museum display about the town's first footbridge. Six glossy photographs showed the mayor at its opening. A seventh picture, printed on rougher paper, showed workers fitting a wooden beam. Their faces were clear, but the mayor was absent. The museum label credited him with building the bridge. Nadia set the picture aside. Before repeating that claim, she wanted to know whether the seventh photograph belonged to the same bridge.
scenes.prompt: Why did Nadia set the seventh photograph aside?

options.text: She wanted to remove every photograph without the mayor
She thought rough paper could not preserve a real photograph
She wanted to check the claim on the museum label

scenes.explanation: The label credits the mayor, but the photograph shows other workers. Nadia wants to check the claim before repeating it.

scenes.title: A Mark in the Wood
scenes.narration: In the gallery, Nadia compared the seventh photograph with a detail photograph of the bridge. Both showed a small triangular notch in the same beam. The picture did belong to this project. A grant ledger recorded the mayor's payment, but said nothing about who did the work. Beside it, a file guide listed construction records and permission letters in the downstairs records room. Nadia realised that paying for a bridge and building it were different kinds of contribution.
scenes.prompt: What did the matching triangular notch establish?

options.text: The construction photograph showed the same bridge
The mayor had personally repaired the beam
The grant payment had never been made

scenes.explanation: The same notch appears in both photographs, linking the construction scene to the bridge in the gallery.

scenes.title: People and Paper
scenes.narration: An assistant recognised one worker in the photograph as Rosa Vale, a retired carpenter who lived across the square. Nadia could visit her and ask what she remembered. She could also follow the file guide to the construction records downstairs. The photograph offered a question, not a complete answer. Nadia wanted to correct the display without replacing one unsupported story with another, so she chose how to gather the missing evidence.
scenes.prompt: What did Nadia want to avoid?

options.text: Learning the names of the bridge workers
Replacing one unsupported account with another
Keeping any record of the mayor's payment

scenes.explanation: Nadia wants evidence, rather than another account that has not been checked.

transitions.label: Visit Rosa Vale and ask about the photograph
Compare the photograph with the construction records

scenes.title: Rosa's Side of the Bridge
scenes.narration: Rosa recognised the photograph immediately. She had cut that beam, while neighbours supplied wood and the mayor paid for the foundations. She showed Nadia her old work diary and agreed to lend both the diary and the photograph to the museum. The revised display gave each contribution its place. Watching Rosa read the new label, Nadia understood that the mystery had not been a missing bridge. It had been the people hidden behind an easy sentence.
scenes.prompt: What did the revised display change?

options.text: It claimed that Rosa had paid for all the foundations
It removed the mayor despite evidence of his payment
It recognised several different contributions to the bridge

scenes.explanation: The display recognises the work, donated wood and foundation funding as different contributions.

scenes.title: The Names below the Grant
scenes.narration: Downstairs, Nadia found signed construction records naming Rosa and the neighbours who had supplied timber. A permission letter allowed the museum to display their work records. The mayor's grant covered the foundations, not the whole project. Nadia prepared a new panel that separated those contributions and sent Rosa a copy before the exhibition. The seventh photograph became its centre. A familiar town story now had enough space for the people who had actually held the tools.
scenes.prompt: Why could Nadia distinguish the mayor's role from Rosa's?

options.text: The records separated foundation funding from construction work
The photograph alone listed every payment
The permission letter said that the grant was imaginary

scenes.explanation: The construction records name the workers, while the grant covers the foundations. They show different roles.

authoringNotes.learningFocus: Comparação de evidências, distinção entre financiamento e execução, e inferência de motivação.

authoringNotes.reviewStatus: Produção e envio à VPS concluídos: WAVs gerados a partir do texto exato e conferidos por transcrição automática; artes 2D dark inspecionadas e corrigidas por cena. Grafo e questões verificados pelos testes. Não declara revisão auditiva humana nem certificação CEFR.
authoringNotes.supportedGameplay: Cenas, narração pré-gravada, uma pergunta por cena, uma bifurcação e dois finais. Objetos, tecnologias e ações são elementos da ficção; não requerem inventário, fala do jogador, combate ou novos eventos de gameplay.
authoringNotes.levelNote: Nível e tamanho são propostas editoriais, não certificação automática CEFR.
humanReviewChecklist: Revisar compreensão e naturalidade do inglês no nível indicado.
Revisar se cada pergunta tem exatamente uma resposta apoiada no texto.
Revisar continuidade, motivação, tom e ambos os finais.
Revisar o registro de autoria e autorização do texto; preencher créditos e evidências das mídias que forem produzidas.
Produzir e escutar WAVs a partir de audioText; revisar e produzir as imagens-base e loops.
Importar como rascunho, validar mídia no servidor e publicar somente após revisão.
